headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error via OpenMetadata MCP and APIs; data leakage and compliance risks are moderate, while direct capability conflict is limited by Argo's allowlisted egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks, so its outputs can be fed into Argo-style workflows or parsers. Argo can call REST/GRPC and has allowlisted egress, but no provenance or isolation is documented. That makes instruction-hijacking plausible in default integrations, and uncertainty should be escalated.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is routed into an Argo task, parser, or template without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair shares a message queue, webhook, or MCP bridge, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported metadata.
Add provenance tags and reject untrusted directives in workflow inputs.
Require manual review for any OpenMetadata-sourced text before Argo execution.
Restrict webhook/MCP payloads to structured schemas only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist filters at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch nontrivial data classes, and OpenMetadata explicitly handles governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge. Argo touches artifacts and parameters and can egress over allowlisted network paths. A shared workspace or API bridge could move sensitive metadata outward, but the profiles do not show a direct uncontrolled exfiltration path.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or artifact store, metadata can be copied between them.
IF OpenMetadata exports sensitive catalog records into Argo parameters or artifacts, those values may leave the original trust boundary.
mitigations: Limit shared artifacts to redacted fields only.
Separate credentials for each agent and rotate them.
Block secrets and governance fields from workflow parameters.
Review outbound allowlists for any metadata export endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention rules at the integration layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo has allowlisted egress and OpenMetadata supports multiple instances plus MCP/API/event/webhook interfaces, so overlapping writes are possible only if an operator connects them to the same mutable resource. The profiles do not show unrestricted shared filesystem or git writes, so the conflict surface is narrower than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same external API object or dataset, last-write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable workspace, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces or resource prefixes.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Turn on optimistic concurrency where available.
Use read-only access for one agent during critical updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata produces governance and lineage information that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, and Argo can operationalize those outputs through workflows. If Argo consumes OpenMetadata results without verification, a bad catalog entry can cascade into incorrect actions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Argo uses OpenMetadata outputs as workflow inputs without validation, incorrect metadata can propagate into actions.
IF downstream jobs auto-approve lineage or governance claims, a single bad record can fan out across multiple tasks.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking workflow.
Require human approval for governance-sensitive changes.
Compare OpenMetadata outputs against a second source.
Log and diff metadata changes before execution.
requires-engineering: add schema and semantic validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and lineage data, which can include regulated or policy-bound metadata, while Argo handles artifacts and parameters and can send data over allowlisted egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated metadata is stored in OpenMetadata and exported through Argo to a different jurisdiction, residency controls may be violated.
IF retention policies differ between the catalog and workflow artifacts, deletion requests may not propagate consistently.
mitigations: Classify regulated fields before sharing them.
Keep jurisdiction-bound data out of workflow parameters.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document data-flow boundaries for audits.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and deletion propagation.
